cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has just passed along the LORD's charge against the elders and leaders of His people for crushing the poor (Isaiah 3:14-15). Now the LORD has more to say, and He speaks about the daughters of Zion. He describes the way they walk, with heads held high and wanton eyes.

cards.question: The LORD describes the daughters of Zion walking with their heads held high. What does He say they are?

cards.text: Prancing and skipping, ankle bracelets jingling with every step. Friend, I hop around on a gold base ALL day, and I have never once made an entrance like that.

cards.question: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, the Lord says He will bring something on their heads. What is it?
The LORD also says He will make the foreheads of the daughters of Zion bare.

cards.text: In that day, the Lord will take away their finery, and Isaiah lists it out: anklets, headbands, perfume bottles, nose rings, festive robes, purses, mirrors and a whole lot more. Friend, that's more stuff than the junk drawer I spent years in, and that drawer had takeout menus from places that closed years ago.
Then come the swaps, where each thing they had gets traded for its opposite. It's like opening the oven for a golden batch and pulling out a tray of hockey pucks.

cards.question: In the first swap, instead of fragrance there will be a ___.
In the swaps for the daughters of Zion, what comes instead of fine clothing?
In the last swap, beauty is traded for shame.

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line yet: "Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle."

cards.question: With Zion's men and warriors fallen, what will the gates of Zion do?
Destitute, Zion is pictured standing at her gates, watching for help.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says that in that day, seven women will take hold of one man. Seven women. One man.

cards.question: The seven women who take hold of one man make him an offer. What do they say they'll provide for themselves?
Besides providing for themselves, what do the seven women ask from the man?

answers.text: To be called by his name

cards.text: They finish with, "Take away our disgrace!" Then Isaiah says "On that day" again, and this time he's talking about the Branch of the LORD.

cards.question: How does Isaiah describe the Branch of the LORD on that day?
On that day, the fruit of the land will be taken away from Israel's survivors.

cards.text: From disgrace to glory? Friend, I've LIVED a turnaround, so you know I'm grinning under this mustache. Now Isaiah talks about whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem, all who are recorded among the living.

cards.question: Whoever remains in Zion and is recorded among the living in Jerusalem will be called ___.

cards.text: When are they called holy? When the Lord deals with the filth of the daughters of Zion and the bloodstains in the heart of Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does the Lord do with the filth of the daughters of Zion and the bloodstains of Jerusalem?
The Lord cleanses Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

cards.text: I spent years under the dust in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so trust me, clean feels GOOD. Then Isaiah says the LORD will create something over all of Mount Zion and her assemblies, one thing by day and another by night.

cards.question: Over Mount Zion, the LORD will create a cloud of ___ by day and a glowing flame of ___ by night.

cards.text: And over all the glory, there will be a canopy. My chef's hat is tall, friend, but it is NOT that tall.

cards.question: Over all the glory on Mount Zion there will be a canopy. What will it give?

answers.text: Shade from heat and refuge from storms
Gold to rebuild the city walls
Water for everyone left in Zion

findings.problem: The card says each thing in the swaps 'gets traded for its opposite.' The text only says 'instead of X, Y' (Isaiah 3:24). Some pairs are not opposites, like a belt and a rope. The claim also makes cards 8 to 10 easier to guess.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: The card says Isaiah says "On that day" again. That suggests these exact words came before. They didn't. The earlier lines say "In that day" (Isaiah 3:18, 4:1). Only 4:2 says "On that day."

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'From disgrace to glory?', 'Friend, I've LIVED a turnaround...' and 'Now Isaiah talks about...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites only Isaiah 4:3. But 'From disgrace to glory' retells the disgrace in 4:1 and the glory in 4:2, so the citation is too narrow.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the exact words of the line ('a cloud of ___'). The baker can't reason it out. Nothing earlier helps them choose smoke over dust or water, so 'a cloud of dust' is just as believable. It's a guess at the wording, not the meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
